summary: This bill amends the Fair Labor Standards Act to exclude employer payments, reimbursements, and the value of services for child or dependent care from the regular rate used to calculate overtime compensation.

scores.thoughts: The bill amends the FLSA solely to change how overtime compensation is calculated by excluding employer-provided child/dependent care benefits. It contains no appropriations, authorizations, or changes to federal spending levels.
No provisions alter tax rates, deductions, credits, or revenue collection.
While elder care is mentioned, the bill addresses labor-law treatment of benefits rather than healthcare delivery, coverage, or markets.
No connection to firearms regulation or rights.
No provisions related to immigration, visas, or border policy.
No provisions concerning reproductive rights or abortion access.
No defense or military spending provisions.
No environmental or regulatory provisions.
The bill facilitates employer-provided care benefits but does not expand, contract, or alter any federal welfare, entitlement, or safety-net programs.
No education funding, school choice, or federal education policy provisions.
No drug enforcement or decriminalization measures.
No criminal sentencing, policing, or justice reform provisions.
No trade, tariff, or globalization provisions.
No deficit, debt ceiling, or fiscal policy provisions.
No provisions affecting LGBTQ legal protections.
No foreign aid or international assistance provisions.
No voting access or election integrity provisions.
No technology regulation or privacy provisions.

The bill directly amends the FLSA to exclude the value of employer-provided child/dependent care from the regular rate used for overtime calculations. This lowers the marginal cost to employers of offering such benefits and increases employer flexibility in structuring compensation packages, aligning modestly with the employer-flexibility end of the spectrum.
No provisions addressing religious exemptions or anti-discrimination rules.
